entry: Chinese strategy for infrastructure and trade connectivity, pursued since 2013. [[Xi Jinping]] first announced it as the [[Silk Road|Silk Road Economic Belt]], and a sea-based 21st-Century Maritime Silk Road was proposed a month later. Projects span ports, railways, highways, power stations, aviation and telecommunications in more than 150 countries. Supporters credit it with closing infrastructure gaps and boosting trade. Critics raise concerns about environmental impact, governance, labor standards and debt sustainability; accusations of "debt-trap diplomacy" are widely disputed by researchers.

Flexible band or strap, worn around the natural waist or hips to keep clothing in place or for aesthetic reasons. Belts are typically made of [[Leather|leather]], plastic or heavy cloth. A buckle often secures the two ends into a loop, though a belt may also be tied with a [[Knot|knot]]. Many garments have belt loops, and a keeper loop stops the free end from flapping. Belts have been documented as men's clothing since the [[Bronze Age|Bronze Age]]. In the western world they have been more common for men, except in the early [[Middle Ages|Middle Ages]] and some other periods. Belts also carry objects such as tools and weapons, and they have been used as whipping weapons and in corporal punishment, sometimes becoming a symbol of child abuse. [[Art Nouveau|Art Nouveau]] belt buckles are now collector's items.

Arctic and sub-Arctic [[Cetacean|cetacean]], the only member of the genus *Delphinapterus*. Its all-white adult coloration and lack of a dorsal fin allow it to swim under ice. A large, deformable melon at the front of the head houses an echolocation organ. Adults reach 5.5 m (18 ft) and weigh up to 1,600 kg (3,530 lb). Belugas usually form groups of about 10 animals, gathering in the hundreds or thousands in summer estuaries. The Cook Inlet subpopulation in Alaska is protected under the U.S. Endangered Species Act.

American actor and filmmaker. Affleck began as a child actor in the [[PBS|PBS]] series *The Voyage of the Mimi*. He and [[Matt Damon|Matt Damon]] won the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Original Screenplay for *Good Will Hunting* (1997), which they co-wrote and starred in. His directorial debut, *Gone Baby Gone* (2007), was well received, and he directed *Argo* (2012), which won the Academy Award for Best Picture. He played Batman in the DC Extended Universe from 2016 to 2023. Affleck co-founded the Eastern Congo Initiative, a grantmaking and advocacy nonprofit.

American neurosurgeon and government official. Carson became the youngest chief of pediatric neurosurgery in the United States in 1984, at the Johns Hopkins Children's Center. In 1987 he led a team in the first-known separation of [[Conjoined twins|conjoined twins]] joined at the back of the head. Nominated by President [[Donald Trump|Donald Trump]], he served as the 17th U.S. Secretary of Housing and Urban Development from 2017 to 2021, after running for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] presidential nomination in 2016. He was named National Nutrition Advisor at the Department of Agriculture in 2025.

1959 American religious epic directed by [[William Wyler|William Wyler]]. Starring [[Charlton Heston|Charlton Heston]] as the Jewish prince Judah Ben-Hur, it adapts Lew Wallace's 1880 novel *Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ*. Its budget of $15.175 million was the largest of any film then produced. The nine-minute chariot race is among cinema's most famous action sequences, and Miklós Rózsa's score was the longest ever composed for a film at the time. The film won a record eleven [[Academy Awards|Academy Awards]], including Best Picture, and was selected for preservation in the National Film Registry of the [[Library of Congress|Library of Congress]] in 2004.

English playwright, poet and actor. Jonson popularized the [[Comedy|comedy]] of humours. He is best known for satirical plays including *Every Man in His Humour* (1598), *Volpone, or The Fox* (c. 1606), *The Alchemist* (1610) and *Bartholomew Fair* (1614), and he is also remembered for his lyric and epigrammatic poetry. He is regarded as the second most important English dramatist of the reign of James I, after [[William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare]]. Classically educated, Jonson served as a volunteer soldier in [[Flanders|Flanders]] before turning to the theater, where he began as an actor. His influence extended to the playwrights and poets of the Jacobean and Caroline eras.

British actor, [[Knight|knighted]] in 2002. Kingsley began in theater with the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1967 and worked mainly on stage for about 15 years. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for playing [[Mahatma Gandhi|Mahatma Gandhi]] in [[Richard Attenborough|Richard Attenborough's]] *Gandhi* (1982). He was Oscar-nominated for *Bugsy* (1990), *Sexy Beast* (2000) and *House of Sand and Fog* (2003), and played Itzhak Stern in [[Steven Spielberg|Steven Spielberg's]] *Schindler's List* (1993). He has played Trevor Slattery in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]], beginning with *Iron Man 3* (2013).

Highest mountain in Scotland and the [[British Isles|British Isles]]. Ben Nevis stands at the western end of the Grampian Mountains near Fort William, in the Highlands. Its summit, 1,345 m (4,413 ft) above sea level, is a stony plateau with the ruins of an [[Observatory|observatory]] staffed from 1883 to 1904. Its meteorological data remains important for understanding Scottish mountain weather, and C. T. R. Wilson was inspired to invent the [[Cloud chamber|cloud chamber]] while working there. An estimated 150,000 visitors climb the mountain each year. The 700-metre (2,300 ft) cliffs of the north face are the principal location in Scotland for ice climbing.

Nigerian-born British poet and novelist. Okri was born in Minna, Nigeria, and spent his early years partly in London before his family moved back to Nigeria in 1966, where his father practised law in [[Lagos|Lagos]]. His exposure to the [[Nigerian Civil War|Nigerian Civil War]] inspired his fiction. He studied comparative literature at the University of Essex. His novel *The Famished Road* won the [[Booker Prize|Booker Prize]] in 1991, making him the youngest winner of the prize. He has been compared to [[Salman Rushdie|Salman Rushdie]] and [[Gabriel García Márquez|Gabriel García Márquez]], and is regarded as one of the foremost African authors in the postmodern and postcolonial traditions. He was knighted in the 2023 King's Birthday Honours for services to literature.

American actor, comedian and filmmaker. Stiller rose to fame in the late 1990s with a group of comic actors known as the Frat Pack. His leading roles include *There's Something About Mary* (1998), *Zoolander* (2001), *Tropic Thunder* (2008) and *Tower Heist* (2011), and he led the *Meet the Parents* and *Night at the Museum* franchises. He made his feature directing debut with *Reality Bites* (1994). Since the mid-2010s he has worked mainly in television, directing and executive producing the Apple TV series *Severance*. He received a Primetime Emmy Award for writing the variety series *The Ben Stiller Show*.

Pakistani stateswoman, prime minister of Pakistan in 1988–1990 and 1993–1996. She was the first woman elected to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority country. Ideologically liberal and secularist, she chaired the Pakistan People's Party from 1982. She studied at [[Harvard University|Harvard University]] and the [[University of Oxford|University of Oxford]], where she was president of the Oxford Union. Her first administration was dismissed in 1990 amid accusations of corruption and nepotism, and her second ended in 1996 when President Farooq Leghari dismissed her government. After returning from exile to contest the 2008 elections, she was assassinated in [[Rawalpindi|Rawalpindi]] after a political rally. The militant group [[Al-Qaeda|al-Qaeda]] claimed responsibility, although other involvement was hypothesized. Critics accused her of inexperience and corruption, but she is regarded posthumously as an icon for [[Women's rights|women's rights]].

American-born British military officer. Arnold fought for the [[American Revolutionary War|Continental Army]], capturing Fort Ticonderoga in 1775 and rising to major general after the Battle of Ridgefield. [[George Washington|George Washington]] gave him command of West Point in July 1780, but Arnold planned to surrender the fort to the British. The plot was exposed when British Major John André was captured with incriminating papers, and Arnold fled to British lines. He was commissioned a brigadier general in the British Army, and his name became synonymous with treason in the United States. He later moved to [[London|London]].

English actor. Cumberbatch won the Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor for *Frankenstein* at the Royal National Theatre in 2011. He gained wide recognition as [[Sherlock Holmes|Sherlock Holmes]] in the [[BBC|BBC]] series *Sherlock* (2010–2017), for which he won a Primetime Emmy Award. He received [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] nominations for playing [[Alan Turing|Alan Turing]] in *The Imitation Game* (2014) and a rancher in *The Power of the Dog* (2021). He has played Doctor Strange in [[Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]] films and portrayed Smaug in *The Hobbit* film series. In 2014, [[Time (magazine)|Time]] magazine named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world.

Italian monk, traditionally known as Saint Benedict. He founded twelve communities for monks at Subiaco before moving southeast to Monte Cassino, where he established the principal abbey. His Rule of Saint Benedict, heavily influenced by the writings of John Cassian, emphasized balance, moderation and reasonableness. It was adopted by most religious communities founded in the [[Middle Ages|Middle Ages]] and became one of the most influential monastic rules in Western Christendom. Giuseppe Carletti regarded him as the founder of Western Christian monasticism. The earliest account of his life is Pope Gregory I's *Dialogues*, a spiritual portrait rather than a modern biography. In 1964 Pope Paul VI declared him a patron saint of Europe. He is revered in the [[Catholic Church|Catholic Church]] and the [[Eastern Orthodox Church|Eastern Orthodox Church]].

Historical and ethnolinguistic region of South Asia, north of the Bay of Bengal. It is divided among [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], the Indian state of West Bengal and Karimganj district in Assam. The Pala Empire was founded there in the 8th century, and an independent Bengal Sultanate later became the eastern frontier of the Islamic world. In 1757 the [[East India Company|East India Company]] defeated the last independent nawab at the Battle of Plassey. Calcutta, now [[Kolkata|Kolkata]], was the capital of Bengal and of India until 1911. Bengali literature, music and cinema are well known in South Asia and beyond.

Population of the tiger subspecies *Panthera tigris tigris* on the [[Indian subcontinent|Indian subcontinent]]. It ranks among the largest wild cats and ranges from India and southern [[Nepal|Nepal]] to [[Bangladesh|Bangladesh]], [[Bhutan|Bhutan]] and southwestern China. The Bengal tiger is the national animal of India and Bangladesh. As of 2022 the population was estimated at 3,167–3,682 individuals in India, 316–355 in Nepal, 131 in Bhutan and around 125 in Bangladesh. It is threatened by poaching, habitat loss and habitat fragmentation.

Capital and largest city of the Indian state of Karnataka, known as Bangalore until 1 November 2014. Called India's "Garden City" for its parks, it lies at about 900 m (3,000 ft) on the [[Deccan Plateau|Deccan Plateau]]. Archaeological artefacts indicate settlement as early as 4000 BCE. The name first appears in an 890 CE Kannada inscription. Kempe Gowda I founded a mud fort in 1537 that is considered the foundation of the modern city. The [[East India Company|British East India Company]] captured the city during the Anglo-Mysore Wars. The 2011 census recorded 8.4 million inhabitants, the third most populous city in India. Bengaluru is a major center for [[Information technology|information technology]] and is often called the [[Silicon Valley|Silicon Valley]] of India.

Second-largest city in Libya and largest in Cyrenaica, on the Gulf of Sidra. It is also a major Mediterranean seaport. A Greek colony named Euesperides existed on the site from around 525 BC, and it was refounded as the Ptolemaic city of Berenice in the 3rd century BC. After around four centuries of Ottoman rule, [[Italy|Italy]] captured the city in 1911 during the Italo-Turkish War. Benghazi was rebuilt after [[World War II|World War II]] and became co-capital of the Kingdom of Libya, but it lost its capital status after the 1969 coup by [[Muammar Gaddafi|Muammar Gaddafi]]. An uprising against Gaddafi began in the city in February 2011, and the National Transitional Council was founded there. Benghazi remains a center of Libyan commerce, industry and culture.

[[Puerto Rico|Puerto Rican]] actor. He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing a police officer in [[Steven Soderbergh|Steven Soderbergh's]] crime drama *Traffic* (2000). After his breakout role in *The Usual Suspects* (1995), he starred in *Sin City* (2005), *Che* (2008) and *Sicario* (2015). He won the Best Actor award at the Cannes Film Festival for *Che*. He played Dario in the [[James Bond|James Bond]] film *Licence to Kill* (1989) and appeared in [[Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]] films. He received a Primetime Emmy Award nomination for the miniseries *Escape at Dannemora* (2018).

Country in West Africa on the [[Gulf of Guinea|Gulf of Guinea]], formerly known as Dahomey. It is bordered by [[Togo|Togo]] to the west, [[Nigeria|Nigeria]] to the east, [[Burkina Faso|Burkina Faso]] to the northwest and [[Niger|Niger]] to the northeast. Porto-Novo is the official capital, and Cotonou is the seat of government and largest city. The economy depends heavily on agriculture, notably palm oil and [[Cotton|cotton]] exports. France incorporated the territory into French West Africa in 1894, and it gained independence in 1960 as Dahomey. It was renamed Benin in 1975, when the People's Republic of Benin was established. A multi-party republic has existed since 1991. The official language is French.

Capital and largest city of Edo State in southern Nigeria. It was the fourth-largest city in Nigeria in the 2006 census, after [[Lagos|Lagos]], [[Kano (city)|Kano]] and [[Ibadan|Ibadan]]. Portuguese visitors arrived around 1485, and the Ọba sent an ambassador to [[Lisbon|Lisbon]] in the early 16th century. The city grew rich through trade in pepper and [[Ivory|ivory]] with Europeans in the 16th and 17th centuries. In 1897 British forces captured, sacked and burned the city after a British delegation was ambushed. The British restored the monarchy in 1914, though political power remained with the colonial administration. After Nigerian independence in 1960 the city became capital of the Mid-Western Region.

Zapotec lawyer and liberal politician, 26th president of Mexico from 1858. He was the first Indigenous president of Mexico and the first democratically elected Indigenous president in postcolonial America. Born in [[Oaxaca|Oaxaca]], he served as governor of Oaxaca and president of the Supreme Court before becoming president. He led the Liberals to victory in the Reform War and in the Second French Intervention, which aimed to install a French-aligned monarchy. His controversial measures included the McLane–Ocampo Treaty, which would have granted the [[United States|United States]] extraterritorial rights across the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, and a decision to seek reelection in 1871, which led [[Porfirio Díaz|Porfirio Díaz]] to rebel. He is considered the most popular Mexican president of the 19th century.

Italian fascist leader, prime minister of Italy from 1922 to 1943 and known as Il Duce. He founded the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento in 1919, which was reorganized as the National Fascist Party in 1921. After the march on Rome, King Victor Emmanuel III appointed him prime minister. Mussolini established the OVRA in 1927 to silence opposition, outlawed strikes and made Italy a one-party state. He signed the Lateran Treaty in 1929, which formally established [[Vatican City|Vatican City]]. His invasion of [[Ethiopia|Ethiopia]] led to condemnation by the [[League of Nations|League of Nations]] and drew him toward [[Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler]] and the Rome–Berlin Axis in 1936. In June 1940 he joined [[World War II|World War II]] on Germany's side. After his removal in 1943 he led the German-backed Italian Social Republic until partisans captured and executed him.

English composer, conductor and pianist. His best-known works include the opera *Peter Grimes* (1945), the *War Requiem* (1962) and *The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra* (1945). He wrote 14 further operas, including the chamber opera *The Turn of the Screw* (1954), and his operas often explore the struggle of an outsider against a hostile society. He wrote much music for children and amateur performers, including *Noye's Fludde*. His most frequent muse was his partner, the tenor Peter Pears, with whom he founded the annual Aldeburgh Festival in 1948. In 1976 he became the first composer to be given a life peerage.
